title: Distance Traveled by a Runner Who Stops to Rest
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: A runner jogs at a steady $8$ miles per hour for the first half hour and then rests completely. Model total distance $d(t)$ after $t$ hours as a piecewise function and find $d(0.4)$ and $d(1)$.

steps.title: Model the Moving Phase
steps.explanation: During the first half hour, distance equals rate times time, the line $d=8t$ rising from $0$ to $4$ miles.
steps.why: Constant speed produces a linear distance function through the origin.

steps.title: Model the Resting Phase
steps.explanation: After stopping, no new ground is covered, so the distance freezes at the $8(0.5)=4$ miles accumulated so far.
steps.why: Zero speed means the distance function becomes constant, not zero.

steps.title: Evaluate Inside the Moving Piece
steps.explanation: The time $t=0.4$ lies in $[0,0.5]$, so the linear branch gives $3.2$ miles.
steps.why: Choosing the correct branch comes down to interval membership of $t$.

steps.title: Evaluate Inside the Constant Piece
steps.explanation: Since $t=1>0.5$, the runner is resting and the total stays at $4$ miles.
steps.why: The flat branch reflects that resting adds no distance no matter how long it lasts.
